page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Advanced Matrix Extensions, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

For storage, the D4ds_v7 includes 236 GB of local disk storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits strong single-threaded performance, achieving top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a notable tradeoff; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth also shows a divergence, with average read-only small block cached bandwidth but weak large-block write bandwidth.

The resource density of 4 vCPUs to 16.0 GB RAM represents a standard general-purpose profile, offering balanced qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that do not require massive parallelization. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations fall into the average tier, indicating suitability for moderate database tasks, static web serving, and general-purpose application hosting. The lack of a GPU and the weak multi-core scaling make it less suitable for heavy parallel computing, but the inclusion of local storage and AMX instructions supports basic vector operations and standard enterprise workloads.

The hardware includes 236 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.
